propositions: transport.py repeatedly hits the 800-line cap, forcing rescue splits that do not solve the underlying growth pattern because new operations have no determined home outside the monolith
previous reactive splits (retry.py, transitions.py) re-exported names as facades, leaving the file's organization unchanged and allowing new capabilities to default back to the same file

the natural architectural seam already exists in _backend.py's capability Protocols (TicketTransport, SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, SupportsAbsenceProbe), which the class satisfies but the file is not organized around
reorganizing transport.py into capability-aligned mixins (_base, _issues, _hierarchy, _links, _people) makes the home of every future operation deterministic by capability, not by available headroom
the relocation must be mechanical (one class composed from mixins, no test assertion edited, no Protocol change) to remain reviewable and preserve isinstance checks and caller contracts
the split must land before further parent-related work (9bb9, 1324) can proceed, and was operator-approved as a separate change
